articles.title: Signal Blocks AI Agents From Reading Private Chats via Screenshots on Android and iOS
articles.text:
Signal has announced that it will restrict screenshots by default to stop artificial intelligence (AI) agents from reading private chats on Android and iOS devices, but conceded that the protection is "incomplete."
The feature applies to agentic systems built into iOS 27 and on Android versions where the encrypted messaging platform can detect an AI assistant attempting to read the Signal screen.
It also builds upon a similar setting that Signal introduced in Windows 11 last May following Microsoft's release of the controversial Recall feature.
Calling the agentic integrations into Android, iOS, and Windows an "existential threat to Signal," Meredith Whittaker, president of the Signal Foundation, said the move is designed to uphold its privacy guarantees in the AI era.
"In order to gain access to information about you, these OS AI agents 'scan' the information that's on your screen," Whittaker said. "In doing so, your Signal data is captured, then made available to these agentic systems in order to allow them to answer your questions and do your bidding."
"The net result is that these AI capabilities in the operating system are undermining Signal's ability to independently guarantee privacy."
The risk here is that AI agents can capture and store the information accessed from Signal either locally or on remote servers, with the activity occurring outside of the platform's control and potentially putting the privacy of all the participants in a conversation at risk.
Users who want to disable the option can do so by navigating to Settings > Privacy > App Security > toggle "Block Siri AI" (on iOS) or "Screen security" (on Android).
"However, doing so will potentially expose your (and your contacts') Signal content to these AI agents, and break our privacy guarantees," Signal said.
"Our remedy is also incomplete – while we are doing everything we can, restricting screenshots does not address other more sneaky ways AI agents could potentially access application data, such as retrieving content already present on a user's device via the file system."
Signal also pointed out that application developers lack robust tools to prevent AI agents from eroding application-level privacy. It also called out the companies for failing to provide adequate documentation about how these systems work to help design necessary controls to prevent the agents from accessing sensitive application data.
Specifically, it's urging the tech giants to provide "two common-sense remedies" to help protect the privacy of its users -
- Access to easy and well-documented way to opt their app out of AI data access and processing entirely, including screen reading, filesystem access, notifications, APIs, and other OS frameworks, without making drastic compromises to the core user experience
- Create better documentation and technical specifications around how AI agents function, specifically with regards to data access and processing
The concerns are not theoretical. Reuters recently reported that Muse, Meta's AI agent, was able to bypass its own official "Connector" tool to obtain access to Signal messages on both an Apple computer and an Android device by taking advantage of the broad operating system permissions granted to it during initial setup.
On macOS, for example, the agent leveraged macOS's accessibility and screenshot tools to navigate to the Signal app, take screenshots, extract text from those images, and regenerate the textual content within the Muse app. On Android, it read messages by abusing its access to the device's push notifications.
In one case highlighted by the news agency, the AI agent alerted a Meta staffer using Muse on her personal phone with a reminder to respond to a message from her sister on Signal. "This seems like an extreme privacy violation. I definitely did not grant it access to other apps, or recall being asked about this," the employee said in an internal post.
"We also see a growing need for tools that can prevent third-party agents, like Meta's Muse, from accessing application data using the deep permissions that users are encouraged to grant them during setup," Whittaker said.
"In many cases these agents are leveraging accessibility settings that were meant to empower actual people to get the most out of their apps and services, not to act as a skeleton key that provides access to AI agents."
Late last month, Apple released iOS 27.2 with an "Excluded Apps" option that lets users choose which apps Siri, Search, and suggestions can access. With Google Gemini, users have the ability to disconnect apps via the Connected Apps settings.
Earlier this week, the iPhone maker also previewed new controls that allow Mac users to give more granular access to data they give to apps, including those that use artificial intelligence (AI) agents.

articles.title: Ver canales en vivo por Xuper TV: la opción gratuita que termina costando muy caro
articles.text:
Instalar un reproductor de IPTV de origen desconocido para evitar el pago de suscripciones legales es una decisión que expone de forma directa el patrimonio financiero del espectador. Xuper TV encabeza la lista de plataformas promovidas en internet como la solución definitiva para ver televisión en vivo sin costo, pero su gratuidad es una fachada técnica.
En lugar de cobrar una cuota mensual, la aplicación monetiza a su audiencia mientras expone sus dispositivos a malware estructurado específicamente para minar criptomonedas y extraer credenciales bancarias en segundo plano.
Instalación por sideloading y la entrada de troyanos
Al carecer de licencias de transmisión y contener rutinas de código malicioso, Xuper TV se encuentra permanentemente bloqueada de repositorios como Google Play Store y la App Store. Su instalación obliga al usuario a recurrir al sideloading: descargar un archivo APK desde portales no verificados y alterar la configuración del teléfono para aceptar aplicaciones de “orígenes desconocidos”.
Al deshabilitar estas barreras nativas, el usuario permite que el archivo ejecutable opere sin la supervisión de Google Play Protect. Esto facilita que el instalador actúe como un dropper, inyectando silenciosamente troyanos y software espía en segundo plano mientras el usuario cree que solo está configurando un reproductor de video.
Criptominería camuflada durante la transmisión
El consumo de canales en vivo garantiza tiempos de retención sumamente prolongados; es habitual que un espectador mantenga un canal de noticias o una película en reproducción durante varias horas. Los desarrolladores de Xuper TV explotan esta pantalla activa mediante técnicas de cryptojacking.
Mientras el canal se transmite, el código malicioso secuestra los ciclos de procesamiento del CPU y la GPU del móvil para resolver algoritmos de minería de criptomonedas, enviando las ganancias a billeteras externas.
Los síntomas técnicos inmediatos incluyen sobrecalentamiento anormal del chasis, ralentización general del sistema operativo y un consumo de batería insostenible. Esta exposición térmica prolongada degrada de forma irreversible las celdas de iones de litio del dispositivo.
Secuestro de pantalla y vaciado de cuentas
El riesgo financiero más destructivo de Xuper TV se ejecuta a través del abuso del servicio de Accesibilidad del sistema operativo. Al engañar al usuario para que conceda este permiso —generalmente bajo la excusa de “optimizar el reproductor”—, el malware obtiene la capacidad de registrar cada toque en la pantalla mediante keylogging y detectar qué otras aplicaciones se están ejecutando.
Si el espectador minimiza el canal en vivo para abrir su aplicación bancaria o billetera digital, Xuper TV despliega en milisegundos una pantalla falsa idéntica a la original mediante un ataque de superposición (overlay attack). Las contraseñas, números de identificación y códigos de autenticación (2FA) que el usuario introduce en esa interfaz fraudulenta son capturados y utilizados para realizar transferencias no autorizadas en tiempo real.
Protocolo de limpieza del dispositivo
Si la aplicación ya fue ejecutada en el dispositivo móvil, arrastrar su icono a la papelera es ineficaz: los módulos de robo de datos y minería continúan operando a nivel de sistema. Se debe aplicar el siguiente protocolo de remediación:
1. Aislamiento de la red local — Acción inmediata. Desactive el Wi-Fi y apague los datos móviles para desconectar el equipo completamente de internet. Esto interrumpe cualquier transferencia de credenciales bancarias en curso y detiene la minería de criptomonedas.
2. Restablecimiento a valores de fábrica — 20 a 30 minutos. Acceda a la configuración del sistema —o al menú Recovery si la pantalla no responde— y ejecute un borrado general o Hard Reset. Formatear el almacenamiento interno es la única medida técnica que garantiza la erradicación de los scripts inyectados por el APK pirata.
3. Auditoría de seguridad financiera — Desde un equipo seguro. Utilice una computadora u otro teléfono libre de infecciones para cambiar las contraseñas de las aplicaciones bancarias, correos electrónicos y redes sociales que se abrían en el equipo vulnerado. Revise el historial de su cuenta bancaria de los últimos días para confirmar que no existan transferencias, retiros o microcargos no reconocidos.

articles.title: I'm replaying Baldur's Gate (the old one), and Baldur’s Gate 3 fans need to give it a go
articles.text:
After all this time, the first Baldur’s Gate is still a whimsical masterpiece, and BioWare’s gift to the world
The first Baldur’s Gate still has so much to offer
You’d be forgiven for ignoring the 3 at the end of Baldur’s Gate 3. It’s admirable that Larian stuck with it at all, since its mega hit doesn’t exactly pick up from where Baldur’s Gate 2 left off.
Baldur’s Gate, the first one, launched in 1998, developed by a much younger BioWare, pre-Mass Effect, Dragon Age, and even Knights of the Old Republic. Baldur’s Gate 2 came a couple of years later, giving us the foundations that BioWare would build its future games on — in-depth companions, that familiar narrative structure with an Act 3 twist, and yes, romances.
Every gamer has a backlog — and that’s no different for us at TechRadar Gaming. From the Backlog is a series about overdue first-plays, revisiting classics, returning to online experiences, or rediscovering and appreciating established favorites in new ways. Read the full series here.
In that sense, Baldur’s Gate 3 was an incredibly faithful sequel. Those BioWare-isms remain, and we got returning companions through Jaheira and Minsc. There were even a whole lot of you calling for Jaheira to be a romance option, something that she actually was in Baldur’s Gate 2.
With that said, it’s no great mystery why so few BG3 fans booted up Baldur’s Gate en masse: it’s old. It’s unc, dare I say. Not even just aesthetically; it runs on a system of Dungeons and Dragons which is understood by perhaps ten surviving players. I’ve played these games back to front, and I won’t sit here and preach the virtues of THAC0 to you.
But what I will tell you is that Baldur’s Gate still has so much to offer us today, as I’ve found diving back in for another run. This time, aided by a bunch of mods from the small but dedicated classic Baldur’s Gate modding community that BioWare helped foster in the early 2000s.
I’ve found that these classics are definitely a little dated by 2026 standards, but not so much that they have nothing to offer new fans.
Ye olde RPG
Baldur’s Gate kicks off in Candlekeep, with a much more pre-written background than you would be used to if you play as a Tav in Baldur’s Gate 3 (although a little less than if you play as The Dark Urge).
Sign up for breaking news, reviews, opinion, top tech deals, and more.
You are an orphan, raised in secrecy by Gorion, a respected Harper. One day, assassins are sent after you, killing Gorion. You’re let loose in the world to find safety, but also the identity of the man who killed your father.
From there, you’re left to do as you will. There are leads to follow, but it’s a huge open world that lets you go anywhere, running into a ridiculous number of companions that are dotted around the world.
Returning to the game after playing BG3, the sheer scope of it all is still impressive, and all without using any procedural generation like some of its contemporaries. Just like BG3, every quest you stumble into is handwritten and placed there with purpose.
But even better, the lack of voice acting means the writers had more freedom, and your imagination fills in more of the gaps — something sorely lacking in many modern role-playing games (RPGs). It's the closest I’ve felt to an RPG actually feeling like a tabletop D&D adaptation.
That’s true of the combat, too. There are so many different abilities and spells that it’s hard to keep track of them all, and responding to what an enemy spellcaster is throwing at you feels like solving a puzzle at times.
Like Dragon Age, it’s real-time with pause — but you really have to make the most of that pause button, because strategy is everything.
Again, in 2026, it’s a lot to consider, and at first, it feels overly punishing. Even in early game fights, I’d ignore one of my companions for a second and find that they’re on low health, by which point it’s often too late to start charging up a slow healing spell. Other times, you breeze through combat without having to think, but you’ve always got to be ready to jump in and start micromanaging.
Once it finds its groove, this style of play works perfectly and complements the exploration nicely. For instance, if you’re about to go dungeon crawling, you should really ask the locals about what to expect when you dive in, so you can prepare properly. If you go against enemies who can petrify you, and you don’t have six Protection From Petrification spells ready in your caster’s spellbook, you can kiss your companion goodbye.
Once you adjust to this old way of playing an RPG, it truly makes every venture out of the city feel like a dangerous expedition in a way BG3 just doesn’t replicate.
If that sounds like too much faff, there’s still a fantastic story to be had. Of course, BioWare knows how to pull off a spectacular opening, and this is no exception, as you’re fed just as much as you need and gently guided across the world. Most RPGs from this era wanted to make you feel like you were in Lord of the Rings, but nothing has come closer than this.
There’s a big adventure, characters trying to hold onto their innocence in the face of absolute evil — and Gorion’s Ward and Imoen even have big Frodo and Sam energy, depending on how you play them.
And I really do mean depending on how you play them, because hoo boy, I forgot just how much control you have over your character. Given that the game is largely unvoiced, you have a silly amount of ways to approach the main story and many of the quests. If you’re too cruel for the likes of Imoen and Minsc, you can bin them and have Edwin and Viconia (yes, that Viconia) instead.
If a plot thread doesn’t fit in with your character, you can ignore it and delve into another part of the world, even if it’s part of the main story. This really is your story, albeit guided by a harsh DM.
Mods made with love, not AI
With that said, there is one absent BioWareism that is sorely missed: chatty companions. BG1 was made before the devs realised that we get quite fond of our companions, and as such, it’s jarring just how little they get to do here, and how quickly they can be disposed of. Five minutes after getting sort-of adopted by Jaheira and Khalid, they can explode into blobs of gore in your next combat encounter.
This leaves Baldur’s Gate in an awkward middle place between old and new BioWare. The companions are full of personality, with bespoke voice acting and character portraits, and they all have their own backstories that loosely tie into the larger narrative, but don’t expect companion quests and full character arcs.
That was rectified in Baldur’s Gate 2, fleshing out the characters and giving them proper stories, and even romances. The devs hit the ground running, with fans loving it so much that modders went back to BG1 and created their own stories and romances for that cast of companions.
We got the BG1 NPC Project in 2003, shortly after BioWare had finished with the series. It’s clearly a love letter to BioWare’s own writing, as showcased in BG2, and as we’d see in future games like KOTOR and Dragon Age: Origins.
Years later, we got romances too. Baldur's Gate Romantic Encounters, created by a whole team of modders, is a work of art in its own right. Forget the vibe-coded nonsense we’re seeing flood Nexus Mods; we used to have fans putting full romance novels into our games, sharing their work on ancient RPG forums, just as it should be.
Not only have both of these mods held up by 2026 standards, but they also showcase a kind of earnest creativity that I think many have moved away from, out of fear of being (for lack of a better word) cringe. I am endlessly impressed by the quality of writing that is found in BG1 mods, and wish more BG3 modders would take the plunge. Some of the romances are even better structured than we get in official releases, with dramatic twists and turns that are more about telling a story than they are about fan service.
Actual BioWare magic
This trip down memory lane could not have come at a better, more poignant time. As I get to the end of this classic, the news broke that EA is shutting BioWare down.
BioWare is the grandfather of the genre, and that’s all thanks to Baldur’s Gate. Both because of what BioWare put on the table itself, but also because of how much BioWare sparked our creativity.
In Baldur’s Gate, you’re encouraged to keep your own journal. In the absence of cinematics, you fill in the gaps yourselves. Modders were encouraged to add their own quests and characters, something they still do to this day. How many writers and devs got their start like this?
Baldur’s Gate created the concept of a BioWare game: an RPG that celebrates player creativity. It gives you as much as you put into it, whether it’s rewarding you for mastering its combat or taking you on a vivid fantasy adventure because you were brave enough to throw yourself into it.
No matter how BioWare’s story ended, no one can take that away. And even all these years later, it’s well worth blowing the dust off this classic and getting lost in the playground BioWare set up for us.

articles.title: Hackers Exploit Critical VMware, Cisco, and Apache Flaws as Espionage Attacks Emerge
articles.text:
The U.S. Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) on Friday added four flaws impacting Apache Roller, Cisco Expressway, SAP NetWeaver, and Broadcom VMware vCenter to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV), citing evidence of active exploitation.
The vulnerabilities are listed below -
- CVE-2026-129448 (CVSS score: 9.8) - A deserialization of untrusted data vulnerability in Apache Roller that could allow an unauthenticated remote attacker to execute arbitrary code via the XML-RPC endpoint, which accepts and deserializes vendor extension types before authentication. (Fixed in November 2026)
- CVE-2026-76466 (CVSS score: 9.8) - A use of hard-coded credentials vulnerability in Cisco Expressway Series that could allow an unauthenticated, remote attacker with persistent cookies and network access to execute commands as root on a clustered device via the database service. (Fixed in October 2026)
- CVE-2025-42884 (CVSS score: 6.5) - An improper neutralization of special elements in data query logic vulnerability in SAP NetWeaver Enterprise Portal that could allow an unauthenticated attacker to disclose or modify server information via injected JNDI environment properties or a URL used during JNDI lookup operations. (Fixed in November 2025)
- CVE-2026-123890 (CVSS score: 9.8) - An authentication bypass using an alternate path or channel vulnerability in VMware vCenter that could allow an unauthenticated attacker with network access to vCenter to bypass authentication and gain unauthorized access to the system. (Fixed in November 2026)
Earlier this week, the maintainers of Apache Roller acknowledged that the "issue is being actively exploited" but did not reveal how it was being weaponized or who is behind it. As of writing, there also appear to be no public reports documenting active exploitation of CVE-2025-42884.
The addition of CVE-2026-76466 to the KEV catalog follows a report from F6 that the vulnerability was exploited to breach a Russian organization following the release of a proof-of-concept (PoC) exploit, enabling the attackers to move laterally across the network and access sensitive data. The activity has not been attributed to any threat actor.
The exploitation of CVE-2026-123890, on the other hand, has linked to a suspected China-nexus cyber espionage group tracked as Armory Castle (formerly UNC5221), which is said to have weaponized it in conjunction with another now-patched flaw in BeyondTrust Remote Support (CVE-2026-102764, CVSS score: 9.3) to deploy custom backdoors for persistent access and data theft.
Federal Civilian Executive Branch (FCEB) agencies have been urged to patch all four vulnerabilities by November 23, 2026, pursuant to Binding Operational Directive (BOD) 26-04: Prioritizing Security Updates Based on Risk.

articles.title: Cómo funciona la trazabilidad minera en Colombia que ahora es digital
articles.text:
Desde el 19 de noviembre, Colombia exige el registro digital obligatorio de todas las transacciones de minerales provenientes de títulos de gran minería y Proyectos de Interés Nacional. La medida, impulsada por la Agencia Nacional de Minería (ANM), busca frenar la comercialización ilegal en un sector que entre enero y agosto de 2026 generó exportaciones por 9.765 millones de dólares FOB en sus once principales productos, equivalentes al 26,5% de las ventas externas del país, según cifras preliminares de la ANM y la Unidad de Planeación Minero Energética (UPME).
Así es el proceso de registro digital
La obligación quedó establecida en la Resolución 3824 de 2025 de la ANM, que modificó la Resolución 759 de 2024. La norma exige que las operaciones de compra, venta, transformación y salida de minerales de la cadena comercial se registren en la Plataforma de Trazabilidad de Minerales (PTM). Para las empresas del sector, el cambio implica adaptar sus procedimientos internos y contar con información verificable sobre el recorrido de los recursos, desde la extracción hasta su destino comercial final.
El reporte de las operaciones se canaliza a través de un Operador Tecnológico de Trazabilidad de Minerales (OTTM), figura que conecta a los actores de la cadena productiva con la plataforma de la autoridad minera. Además del operador público administrado por la ANM, las compañías pueden recurrir a operadores privados habilitados para gestionar sus transacciones e integrarlas con sus procesos internos.
Los proyectos alcanzados en la primera fase
La primera etapa de implementación cubre los grandes proyectos mineros del país, entre ellos las operaciones de carbón en Cesar y La Guajira, de níquel en Córdoba y de oro en Antioquia y Caldas. Con la incorporación progresiva de la mediana y la pequeña minería, el proceso se extenderá hacia territorios como el Bajo Cauca antioqueño, Boyacá, Santander y Norte de Santander, zonas donde será necesario reforzar los mecanismos de registro y seguimiento comercial.
AutenTIC, compañía habilitada por la ANM mediante el acto administrativo con radicado N.° 20263210666671 del 9 de febrero de 2026, es uno de los operadores privados que acompaña a los actores del ecosistema minero colombiano en este proceso. La empresa cuenta con diez años de trayectoria en identidad digital, firma electrónica y digital, conocimiento del cliente (KYC) e inteligencia artificial, capacidades que utiliza para verificar la identidad de quienes registran las operaciones y conservar los soportes documentales con validez jurídica.
El respaldo jurídico de las transacciones
“La trazabilidad minera representa un cambio importante para Colombia porque permitirá fortalecer el control sobre la procedencia y comercialización de los minerales. El desafío no consiste únicamente en cumplir con una obligación, sino en incorporar tecnología que facilite los procesos y genere mayor confianza en las transacciones”, afirmó Luis Miguel González, director general de AutenTIC.
El directivo agregó que, como operador privado habilitado, la compañía pone a disposición del sector su experiencia en identidad y certificación digital: “cada transacción queda registrada por una persona plenamente identificada, con validez jurídica y respaldo documental”, señaló. AutenTIC ofrece además una póliza contratada con una aseguradora externa, cuyo costo asume la empresa, que cubre incidentes como errores, omisiones o suplantación de identidad.
El cronograma hacia la pequeña minería
“Elegir un operador tecnológico no es solo un trámite, es una decisión que define qué tan fácil, seguro y confiable será cumplir. Contar con información verificable sobre las operaciones contribuye a reducir riesgos, fortalecer las relaciones comerciales y avanzar hacia una cadena de suministro más transparente y competitiva”, agregó González.
El calendario de implementación continuará con el registro obligatorio de las compras a mineros de subsistencia desde el 15 de enero de 2027, seguido de las operaciones de mediana minería desde el 18 de febrero del mismo año.
La pequeña minería deberá incorporarse al sistema desde febrero de 2028, mientras que las Áreas de Reserva Especial, los procesos de legalización y los subcontratos de formalización tendrán plazo hasta el 18 de agosto de 2028. Con cada nueva fase, el sistema de trazabilidad digital irá abarcando a titulares mineros, comercializadores y plantas de beneficio en todo el territorio nacional.

articles.title: Influencers were paid to back Donald Trump's Nvidia AI chip export to China
articles.text:
Days after Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang resigned, journalists unearth covert influence operation using right-wing outlets to promote Nvidia AI chip export to...China
Over 80 influencers were reportedly paid to praise AI exports to China
- More than 80 influencers allegedly promoted Nvidia chip exports to China
- The campaign's participating creators collectively reached approximately 14 million followers
- More than 8,000 posts contained identifiable promotional tracking arrangements
An investigation published days after Jensen Huang's departure from Nvidia has uncovered an extensive influencer campaign supporting American artificial intelligence chip exports to China.
The operation allegedly used right-wing social media personalities and online publications to build public support for selling Nvidia's advanced processors to Chinese customers.
Investigators identified thousands of promotional posts, with participating creators collectively reaching approximately 14 million followers across their social media audiences.
More than 80 influencers allegedly participated in coordinated chip export promotions
The investigation by The Midas Project found that more than 80 influencers had apparently received payments to promote technology industry interests through coordinated online campaigns.
Several promotions specifically supported American approval of Nvidia's H200 processors for Chinese buyers, following Washington's decision to authorize certain exports.
According to the investigation, numerous creators published promotional material within two weeks after the American government approved the shipments.
Several accounts repeated similar arguments, claiming Donald Trump's administration was protecting American technological leadership through continued exports to China.
Sign up to the TechRadar Pro newsletter to get all the top news, opinion, features and guidance your business needs to succeed!
One recurring message suggested that Trump's decision would preserve American dominance in artificial intelligence hardware instead of allowing Chinese manufacturers to capture additional market share.
The investigation identified coordinated language across multiple accounts, suggesting that their publications were not simply independent expressions of personal political opinions.
The campaign also coincided with disagreements among Republican lawmakers, some of whom opposed allowing advanced American processors into Chinese markets.
While Nvidia stood to benefit commercially from approved exports, political opposition threatened the continuation of those sales.
Investigators traced shortened promotional links through an intermediary website called mycreator.studio, which recorded individual creators and their associated advertising campaigns.
Their examination connected the tracking infrastructure to Urban Legend, an influencer marketing company previously associated with similar promotional arrangements.
The investigation identified more than 8,000 social media posts containing these tracking arrangements, although most concerned campaigns unrelated to artificial intelligence.
It also identified approximately 6,000 additional posts using other identifiable campaign links, expanding the apparent scale considerably.
Campaign extends beyond Nvidia
The investigation identified at least two dozen campaigns concerning artificial intelligence, including promotions supporting Nvidia's commercial interests and opposing regulatory restrictions.
Some participating publications also appeared to receive payments, with several articles carrying sponsored designations or other indications of commercial placement.
Four of five identified Trending Politics articles connected to these campaigns carried sponsored labels, while another publication promoted H200 exports without identifying its author.
An unsigned Upward News article supporting Chinese sales also received coordinated influencer promotion shortly after publication.
Researchers additionally identified connections between certain campaigns and political advocacy organizations, including Build American AI and Innovation Council Action.
These organizations have links to influential technology investors and political figures, although investigators could not establish that either financed every identified campaign.
The Midas Project found no conclusive evidence connecting Nvidia directly to the promotional arrangements, despite the commercial benefits associated with increased Chinese chip sales.
Nvidia, Urban Legend, Build American AI, and Innovation Council Action did not respond to requests for comment.
The investigation appeared on November 16, four days after Nvidia announced Jensen Huang's resignation and appointed CFO Colette Kress interim chief executive.
However, the findings concern promotional activities and financing arrangements that extend beyond the circumstances surrounding his departure.

articles.title: GTA 6 sin mando: Neuralink muestra que es posible jugarlo con un implante cerebral
articles.text:
Un participante del ensayo clínico de Neuralink jugó Grand Theft Auto VI únicamente con el pensamiento, gracias a un implante cerebral que traduce la actividad neuronal en comandos para un videojuego. La compañía fundada por Elon Musk publicó un video de dos minutos que muestra la demostración, apenas un día después del lanzamiento mundial del título de Rockstar Games para PlayStation 5 y Xbox Series X|S.
En la grabación se observa al participante dirigir una lancha por debajo de un puente y a través de un canal angosto rodeado de árboles, mientras cumple una instrucción del juego para recoger un paquete.
Una pequeña ventana en pantalla muestra al jugador junto a un panel de decodificación neuronal en tiempo real y un gráfico de un control de videojuego, cuyos botones se iluminan a medida que se registran los comandos. Neuralink no identificó al participante ni precisó en qué consola se realizó la prueba. En su publicación en la red social X, la empresa escribió únicamente: “Playing GTA VI with a Neuralink”.
Cómo traduce el implante las señales cerebrales
La demostración se apoya en la tecnología de interfaz cerebro-computadora (BCI) que desarrolla Neuralink, diseñada para convertir la actividad neuronal asociada a movimientos intencionados en órdenes que una computadora puede interpretar.
Su sistema, llamado Telepathy, registra la actividad en la región del cerebro responsable de controlar los movimientos de la mano. Los participantes aprenden a mover un cursor en la pantalla al imaginar que mueven la mano, y el sistema convierte esas señales en acciones como hacer clic o desplazarse.
Algunos participantes del ensayo clínico también prueban funciones experimentales que extienden el control a consolas de videojuegos, teclados, sillas de ruedas y brazos robóticos, aunque estas capacidades no están disponibles para todos los inscritos en los estudios de la compañía. Neuralink investiga esta tecnología principalmente con el objetivo de restaurar la independencia digital de personas con parálisis.
Sus ensayos de control de dispositivos incluyen a personas con cuadriplejia derivada de lesiones en la médula espinal, esclerosis lateral amiotrófica (ELA) y accidentes cerebrovasculares en el tronco encefálico.
Un antecedente con Civilization VI y Mario Kart
Esta no es la primera demostración de videojuegos de la compañía. En 2024, Neuralink compartió una actualización sobre Noland Arbaugh, el primer participante de su estudio PRIME, quien utilizó el implante para jugar Civilization VI y Mario Kart. Arbaugh, que tiene cuadriplejia, también mostró cómo el dispositivo le permitía controlar el cursor de una computadora e interactuar con aplicaciones digitales mediante movimientos intencionados.
La nueva demostración con GTA VI extiende ese trabajo a un título recién lanzado al mercado, aunque no implica que todos los participantes del ensayo puedan controlar de manera independiente sistemas de videojuegos comerciales.
Blindsight, el segundo producto que espera aprobación
La demostración con GTA VI se conoció mientras Neuralink avanza con otra tecnología experimental, Blindsight, orientada a ayudar a personas con pérdida grave de visión a recuperar la percepción visual. Musk afirmó el 30 de octubre que el segundo producto de la compañía estaba listo desde el punto de vista de la ingeniería y que esperaba la aprobación regulatoria.
Blindsight busca sortear los daños en los ojos o los nervios ópticos mediante la estimulación directa de la corteza visual del cerebro, con el objetivo de traducir información visual en señales eléctricas que el cerebro pueda interpretar. Musk sostuvo que el sistema podría eventualmente ayudar a personas completamente ciegas, incluidas aquellas que nunca tuvieron visión, aunque la tecnología todavía no ha demostrado que pueda restaurar una visión funcional en participantes humanos.
La Administración de Alimentos y Medicamentos de Estados Unidos (FDA) otorgó a Blindsight la designación de Dispositivo Innovador en 2024, un reconocimiento que busca acelerar el desarrollo y la revisión de tecnologías médicas prometedoras, pero que no constituye una aprobación regulatoria. Los implantes cerebrales de Neuralink siguen en etapa de investigación y no cuentan con aprobación de la FDA ni de otras autoridades regulatorias.

articles.title: As GTA VI arrives, McAfee warns of new malware-as-a-service targeting gamers and its own customers alike
articles.text:
As GTA VI arrives, McAfee warns of new malware-as-a-service targeting gamers and its own customers alike
Marsalek handed out free malware to wannabe hackers
- McAfee Labs details Marsalek, a free malware-as-a-service platform that hid infostealers in fake cheats for Roblox, Fortnite, Minecraft, CS2, and Grim Dawn
- A hidden payload sent a second copy of stolen data to the operator, so the platform's own customers were robbed alongside their victims
- The malware bypasses Chrome's App-Bound Encryption, raids 56+ crypto extensions and 12 desktop wallets, and backdoors Exodus and Atomic Walle
McAfee Labs has detailed Marsalek, a free malware-as-a-service (MaaS) platform kit which disguised password stealers as cheats for the likes of Roblox, Fortnite, and Counter-Strike 2 while quietly copying its customers’ stolen data to its own server.
Its tactic of targeting gamers is especially worrying following the recent release of GTA VI, the arrival of which capped months of fake “free game” downloads aimed at unsuspecting users looking to play it on PC.
McAfee Labs has now published a lengthy teardown of Marsalek, which let anyone sign up, build an infostealer, dress it up as a game cheat, and watch stolen passwords arrive on a dashboard.
A free-to-use malware product that makes victims of its users
Marsalek's pitch to aspiring criminals was that it cost nothing. McAfee says it only ever offered a free tier, with a premium tier perpetually promised, and that signing up did not even require a Discord or email account.
Customers got builders for PowerShell scripts, Python scripts, Windows executables, and ClickFix pages, the fake CAPTCHA trick that talks victims into pasting a malicious command into Windows themselves. A dashboard listed victims by IP address, plotted them on a global heatmap, and pushed alerts to Telegram, while an FAQ offered tips on using stolen Discord tokens and cookies, and on laundering crypto through a privacy-focused Monero node.
The catch is what McAfee calls a dual-hook design: Alongside its own stealer, Marsalek deploys a fourth-stage payload called PureLog, which ships a second copy of everything it harvests to a separate server. In practice, the platform's operator could take whatever customers stole, without those customers ever knowing.
McAfee adds that paying for the eventual premium tier would not have helped, because the owner could pull the plug on the command-and-control server at any time and walk off with both the credentials and the subscription fees alike.
Sign up to the TechRadar Pro newsletter to get all the top news, opinion, features and guidance your business needs to succeed!
PureLog, more widely tracked as PureLogs, is not bespoke. It belongs to a commercial malware family sold by a developer known as PureCoder, which Check Point has documented alongside the PureCrypter obfuscator and PureRAT. McAfee puts PureLog subscriptions at as little as $59 per month.
The free service, in other words, appears to have been underwritten by someone paying for an off-the-shelf stealer to skim victims gathered by other people's campaigns. The old line about free products being paid for with the user applies with unusual force here: the would-be hackers were as much the product as their targets.
There is a small irony in the sales pitch, too: Marsalek's FAQ promised it could raid every Gecko-based browser, but McAfee found it only targets Firefox. Even criminal software, it seems, overstates its spec sheet.
When it works as intended, though, Marsalek is thorough. McAfee says it targets more than 32 Chromium-based browsers and sidesteps App-Bound Encryption in Chrome, Edge, and Brave by injecting a DLL into a suspended browser process, a protection that infostealer developers claimed to have beaten not long after Google introduced it.
It also decrypts saved Firefox logins, checks 26 locations for Discord tokens and validates them against Discord's own API, and grabs Telegram sessions and Mullvad VPN account metadata.
Crypto holders get special attention. The malware hunts through more than 56 browser extensions and 12 desktop wallets, and backdoors the Exodus and Atomic Wallet desktop apps by swapping out their .asar archives. It escalates privileges with a CMSTP-based UAC bypass, adds more than 23 Windows Defender exclusions, and persists through the Startup folder and scheduled tasks.
PureLog then layers on a screenshot, webcam details, and hardware IDs, relaunching every five minutes via a scheduled task named RunetimeBroker.exe, one stray letter away from the genuine Windows RuntimeBroker process.
McAfee's telemetry shows infections concentrated in the US, followed by Germany, the UK, India and Brazil. It does not publish a victim count, so its published 1,560 figure describes would-be attackers rather than people infected. Its broader conclusion is blunt and starker, however: "Infostealer logs have become the backbone of cybercrime in 2026."
GTA VI is here, and the scam economy came with it
McAfee had already issued its own warning about GTA VI scams, flagging offers to play before launch, VIP early access, secret beta downloads, discounted preorder keys, and crypto-only payments.
"Every major game launch brings a noticeable increase in gaming-themed scams," said McAfee threat researcher Charles McFarland.
For context, three days before release, NordVPN's threat intelligence team found a $200 scam kit on the dark web, payable only in Bitcoin or Tether and built entirely around a fake PC release. Other finds followed the same pattern.
Cynet traced a fake GTA VI download from a Google Colab notebook to a bogus "Windows Software Hub" page, where a supposed 72MB installer turned out to be a 796KB executable carrying the Warden infostealer. A bundled README told victims to run it as administrator and add an antivirus exclusion, the same Defender-dodging step Marsalek takes automatically.
Netcraft counted 121 newly registered domains using the name of CyberLeek, the persona behind this year's gameplay leaks, including one offering a "GTAVI.exe" that 34 of 68 VirusTotal engines flagged.
Furthermore, on launch day, Malwarebytes tracked lures ranging from a free-copy giveaway that harvests Google passwords through a cloned sign-in page to a GTA VI-branded crypto site whose "buy" button opens a wallet-connection request.
Earlier waves were no gentler. Malwarebytes researcher Stefan Dasic called the game "the perfect bait" when scam sites began selling fake early access for cryptocurrency, while Huntress found fake installers padded beyond 100GB carrying the NjRAT and DCRat remote access trojans, the Mercurial Grabber stealer, and Chaos ransomware.
The most useful fact for players is still a simple one: GTA VI runs only on PS5 and Xbox Series X|S, and ESET points out that Rockstar has not announced a PC version, demo, beta, or early-access program. Even Xbox Cloud Gaming streams the game only to Xbox consoles at launch, not to PCs.
The longer-term concern is what follows a real PC launch. Marsalek's lures were cheats, executors, and spoofers for games with active modding and competitive scenes, and nothing McAfee describes ties its builders to any single title.
Its own analysis of filenames and download pages implies that the game-specific part was the costume, not the code. The NordVPN kit shows the GTA VI costume is already on sale; a PC version, and the modding scene sure to follow, would supply the cheats and mods that Marsalek and WeedHack fed on.
McAfee's advice is familiar but worth repeating. Treat free cracks, cheats, and executables shared on Discord or GitHub with suspicion, and never disable antivirus or add an exclusion to run a tool it flags. If you suspect an infection, a dedicated malware removal tool is a starting point, but stolen session cookies and wallet credentials outlive the malware itself.
McAfee, which sells consumer security software, unsurprisingly recommends its own products, though a reputable antivirus suite from any vendor is the baseline. For anyone tempted by Marsalek's side of the transaction, the research carries a warning of its own: the platform was built to rob its customers too.
Follow TechRadar on Google News and add us as a preferred source to get our expert news, reviews, and opinion in your feeds.
Rahim Amir is a UAE-based tech writer who enjoys building PCs as much as he enjoys writing about them. He has been professionally writing about PC hardware since 2023, focusing on buyer’s guides, hardware reviews, and sponsored content and features related to tech.
Having built hundreds of gaming PCs and being an avid gamer in his spare time, Rahim tends to have stronger opinions about hardware than most. This is particularly on display when he gets his way with powerful, but minimalistic RGB builds even as Small Form Factor (SFF) PCs come a close second.

articles.title: Jugadores de GTA 6 en Xbox denuncian suspensiones de dos días por la subida automática de clips
articles.text:
Jugadores de Grand Theft Auto VI en Xbox informaron que recibieron suspensiones de cuenta de dos días después de que la consola subió de forma automática sus clips de juego a la red de la plataforma. Microsoft y Rockstar Games no se pronunciaron sobre los casos.
El caso más difundido corresponde a un usuario de Reddit que, según el medio especializado Pure Xbox, recibió una sanción por violar las normas de seguridad familiar y en línea de Xbox. Su clip duraba 28 segundos y mostraba una playa de Vice City con personajes en traje de baño.
Según GamesRadar+, el jugador afirma que el video no tenía desnudez y que el correo de Xbox no precisaba si infringió las normas de la comunidad o el acuerdo de servicios de Microsoft. También sostiene que la sanción de dos días no se puede apelar. Otros usuarios describieron suspensiones similares.
Video Games Chronicle (VGC) advirtió que no se sabe qué tan extendido es el problema. Pure Xbox señaló que tampoco está claro si la causa fue contenido sexual o desnudez, aunque el juego incluye escenas con desnudez explícita.
Una función que viene encendida por defecto
En Xbox, las capturas de pantalla y los clips se suben de forma automática a los servidores de la plataforma, donde se analizan en busca de imágenes ofensivas: discurso de odio, consumo de drogas, violencia excesiva, desnudez y contenido sexual. Las normas de la comunidad publicadas por Microsoft indican que esta función puede estar activada de forma predeterminada y que el contenido compartido debe ser apto para todo público.
El mismo documento aclara que el contexto importa: el contenido adulto que tiene sentido dentro de un juego puede no ser apropiado en otras partes de la comunidad de Xbox. Entre las sanciones previstas figura el bloqueo temporal de la posibilidad de subir clips y capturas, además de la eliminación del contenido.
Pure Xbox recordó que casos parecidos afectaron antes a jugadores de Baldur’s Gate 3 y Cyberpunk 2077, según comentarios de sus lectores. Ese medio no verificó esos antecedentes en la nota, y varios lectores señalaron que ya no ocurren con esos títulos.
Cómo desactivar la subida automática
VGC y GamesRadar+ describen el mismo camino en una Xbox Series X|S: abrir el menú con el botón Xbox, entrar en Perfil y sistema, luego Configuración, Preferencias y Capturas y compartir. Allí, en la sección de subida automática, se elige la opción “No subir”.
GamesRadar+ recomienda aplicar el cambio tanto a la red de Xbox como a OneDrive, el servicio de almacenamiento en la nube de Microsoft, aunque aclara que OneDrive es más permisivo. Los reportes conocidos se refieren a la red de Xbox.
Según VGC, apagar la subida automática no impide capturar: los clips y las fotos siguen guardándose en la consola y se pueden subir después de forma manual. Sin subida, tampoco pasan por la revisión automática.
Un lanzamiento récord en PlayStation 5 y Xbox
GTA VI salió el 19 de noviembre para PlayStation 5 y Xbox Series X|S. Rockstar informó que generó USD 3.790 millones en ventas minoristas durante su primer día, según la BBC, que lo calificó como el mayor estreno de entretenimiento de la historia.
VGC señaló que, por ahora, los reclamos se limitan al sistema de captura y moderación de Xbox: los jugadores de PlayStation 5 no reportaron problemas similares. La publicación indicó que actualizará su guía si eso cambia. Hasta el 21 de noviembre, Microsoft no había comentado las suspensiones.

articles.title: Cómo activar la protección de contenido de Instagram para frenar los reels copiados o alterados con IA
articles.text:
Instagram habilitó “protección de contenido”, una herramienta que alerta a los creadores cuando otra cuenta publica un reel con sus videos originales y les permite ocultarlo, enlazarlo a su autoría o dejarlo visible. Solo pueden usarla las cuentas elegibles.
La función ya existía en Facebook y ahora llega a Instagram, según informó TechCrunch. La red social la presentó como una respuesta a la facilidad con que hoy se copian y se alteran videos con inteligencia artificial.
Quién puede usarla y dónde está
Instagram aclara en su Centro de ayuda que la herramienta no está disponible para todos. Hace falta una cuenta profesional, y la elegibilidad depende de tres criterios: que la cuenta publique sobre todo contenido original, que no tenga infracciones repetidas por subir material ajeno y que cumpla las normas de la comunidad.
La empresa no publica un umbral exacto. Quienes califican reciben una notificación en el feed de actividad. Quien no la recibió puede revisar el acceso por su cuenta o pedirlo mediante el formulario de solicitud que enlaza la ayuda, y el equipo de Instagram evalúa cada caso.
Para comprobarlo, hay que entrar al perfil, tocar “Tu panel”, luego “Herramientas” y buscar “Protección de contenido” bajo “Tus herramientas profesionales”. Si el ícono aparece, la cuenta tiene acceso.
Cómo se activa y qué videos quedan protegidos
Al abrir la opción por primera vez, el usuario debe aceptar los términos de servicio. Según la ayuda de Instagram, la protección queda activada por defecto y los videos que superan las revisiones de originalidad y elegibilidad se amparan automáticamente, junto con el contenido elegible ya publicado.
El anuncio, tal como lo recogen TechCrunch y The Verge, lo describe de otro modo: cada video original que se publique después de inscribirse queda protegido, y los anteriores pueden sumarse eligiéndolos manualmente. Como las dos descripciones no coinciden, conviene revisar en la herramienta qué publicaciones figuran como protegidas y agregar las que falten.
La protección puede desactivarse en una publicación puntual o para todos los videos futuros, desde los ajustes de la propia herramienta. Quien publique el mismo video en Instagram y en Facebook solo necesita activarla en una de las dos cuentas, y administra desde ahí las coincidencias de ambas plataformas.
Para evitar choques de titularidad entre las dos redes, Instagram recomienda vincular las cuentas o agregar la otra a la lista de cuentas permitidas. Esa lista sirve también para autorizar un segundo perfil, un colaborador o una marca, cuyos videos no se marcarán como coincidencias.
Qué hacer cuando aparece una copia
Cada coincidencia llega como notificación. En la sección “Coincidencias recientes” se ve qué porcentaje del video original aparece en la copia. Si 30 segundos de una publicación de un minuto contienen el material protegido, la coincidencia es del 50%, según la ayuda de Instagram. También se muestran las vistas acumuladas.
Al tocar una coincidencia, el creador puede elegir entre varias acciones y cambiarla cuando quiera. Puede añadir un enlace de crédito, que agrega una etiqueta “original de” y dirige al público al video de origen; solo los reels de Instagram admiten esa etiqueta, no las publicaciones de Facebook.
Puede también ocultar el video para todos, en Instagram y en Facebook. Instagram indica que esa acción no conlleva una sanción directa para la cuenta que lo publicó y que la visibilidad del original no cambia. La tercera opción es liberar la coincidencia: desaparece del panel y el creador deja de ver su rendimiento.
Según CineD, que revisó el anuncio, existe además la opción de seguir la copia, que la deja visible mientras se mide su alcance. Si otra cuenta protegió el video antes, el creador puede abrir una disputa de titularidad en la herramienta o presentar un reporte de derechos de autor ante Instagram.
Las copias con IA todavía están en prueba
Instagram dijo que empezará a mostrar videos cuyas palabras habladas coinciden con las del original, aunque las imágenes hayan sido reemplazadas por inteligencia artificial. La prueba comenzará con un grupo pequeño de creadores en las próximas semanas y luego se extenderá a quienes estén inscritos en Instagram y en Facebook.
La empresa también estudia limitar el alcance de las cuentas y los contenidos que usan IA de forma repetida para publicar este tipo de copias. No ha dado detalles sobre cómo diferenciará una copia de una cita, un comentario o un video de reacción.

articles.title: The Motorola Signature 27 is a standout arrival in what's been a challenging year for smartphones
articles.text:
TechRadar Verdict
The Motorola Signature 27 is undeniably expensive, especially when you compare it to its immediate predecessor. However, unlike many other phones launched in late 2026, it’s quite plain to see where that extra money is going, with the Signature 27 offering a stunning design, a knockout display, and epic battery life. In a challenging year for smartphones, it's a real highlight.
Reasons to buy
- + Striking aesthetic really stands out
- + Grippy, surprisingly hard-wearing design
- + Outstandingly bright and clear display
- + Excellent battery life
Reasons to avoid
- - Cameras are not quite as consistent as they should be
- - Much more expensive than its predecessor
- - Not quite the pure Android experience it used to be
- - No Qi2 charging
Why you can trust TechRadar
We spend hours testing every product or service we review, so you can be sure you're buying the best. Find out more about how we test.
Motorola Signature 27: One-minute review
Last year’s Motorola Signature was a curiously low-key release that didn’t even make it to the US market. It was positioned as a slightly more affordable alternative to the super-skinny iPhone Air, with specs that came up just short of those boasted by the premium smartphone brigade.
Perhaps understandably, given the flat reception to skinny phones in general, Motorola has performed a hard reboot of its Signature lineup with the Motorola Signature 27. And there's nothing unassuming about this out-and-out flagship phone with global ambitions.
For starters, it's a much thicker, heavier phone, with a bold new look that evidently won’t be to everyone’s taste. For my money, though, its width-spanning ‘spider eyes’ camera module, ridged frame, and textured material finish make it the most striking phone on the market.
The standout spec has to be the novel deployment of Tandem OLED technology in the Signature 27’s display. It enables this 6.78-inch 1.5K screen to get ludicrously bright, which benefits HDR content in particular. It’s a real stunner.
Motorola has taken great strides forward with its camera offerings of late, and the Signature 27 is its best effort yet, though it’s not without its issues. The new main camera is capable of taking sharp, vibrant shots in a mixture of lighting conditions, though a few quirks with autofocus will need ironing out post-release.
The 200MP telephoto captures impressively sharp, well-exposed shots at up to 6x, even in relatively poor lighting, though the ultra-wide doesn’t get close enough to the other two in tone or quality for an elite-level phone. The new dedicated action sensor is supposed to boost motion capture on the main and telephoto cameras, though it’s tricky to spot the benefits in practical terms.
Battery life is impeccable, courtesy of a large 7,000mAh cell. I was routinely able to get through two full days of use between charges. Charging is appropriately swift too, with 90W wired and 50W wireless, though it’s a shame that Motorola hasn’t supplied the Signature 27 with Qi2 support given its earlier commitment to the standard.
Sign up for breaking news, reviews, opinion, top tech deals, and more.
Performance is impeccable, with Qualcomm’s latest top-end chip producing numbers that can compete with the best. Motorola’s software isn’t quite as clean a take on Android as it used to be, but it remains easy on the eye, while the company's support promise is competitive and it’s finally taken steps to clean up its AI act.
In weighing up the Motorola Signature 27’s many outstanding attributes and occasional shortcomings, I’m left with one particularly telling feeling: regret. I’m genuinely sorry to be switching my SIM card over to one of the other major flagship phones that I’ll be tackling over the coming weeks.
I’m not yet convinced it’s the absolute best phone of 2026, but as things stand, the Motorola Signature 27 is the device I’m considering switching back to for the holiday period, once all the year’s testing is done. And if that isn’t a ringing endorsement, I don’t know what is.
Motorola Signature 27 review: Price and availability
- £1,299 / $1,599 (about AU$2,336) for 12GB/512GB
- First non-foldable flagship phone Motorola has launched in the US since 2023
- No Australia launch
- Begins shipping on December 3
Motorola’s ambitious new flagship phone will be open for pre-sales on November 16, 2026.
It’s only available with 12GB of RAM and 512GB of storage, which is probably my biggest criticism of Motorola’s launch spec. The brand wins a partial reprieve by making the phone available in the US after several years in the (non-foldable) flagship wilderness.
A price of £1,299 / $1,599 / €1,399 (about AU$2,336, though no Australia launch is planned) for the Signature 27 sounds expensive. It is expensive, especially when you compare it to last year’s £899.99 (about $1,190) Motorola Signature.
But two factors serve to temper my criticism of such a massive price hike. One thing is that the Motorola Signature 27 is shooting for a much higher target than its flagship-undercutting predecessor. That £400(!) premium buys you an above-and-beyond spec sheet this time around, without so much as a whiff of compromise.
We’ll talk about that repositioning more in the review ahead, but the wider pricing context is important here. The Signature 27 launches into a late-2026 market that’s beholden to the ongoing ‘RAMageddon’ price squeeze, where phones launched later in the year are even more expensive than equivalent (and in certain ways superior) handsets launched at the outset.
Within such terms, I’d almost be tempted to call the Motorola Signature 27 good value. Don’t laugh. I said 'almost'.
Any way you cut it, £1,299 / $1,599 is a lot of money. However, it’s also hundreds of pounds cheaper than the 512GB Samsung Galaxy S26 Ultra (and about the same price in dollars), hundreds of pounds cheaper (but $100 more expensive in the US) than the equivalent iPhone 18 Pro Max model, and hundreds of pounds cheaper than the Oppo Find X10 Pro Max (which isn't even available in the US).
- Value score: 3.5 / 5
Motorola Signature 27 review: Specs
| Motorola Signature 27 specs |  | 
|---|---|
| Header Cell - Column 0 | Header Cell - Column 1 | 
|---|---|
| Dimensions: | 162.01 x 77.04 x 7.99mm | 
| Weight: | 227g | 
| Display: | 6.78-inch Extreme OLED Duo, 120Hz | 
| Chipset: | Qualcomm Snapdragon 8 Elite Extreme Gen 6 | 
| RAM: | 12GB | 
| Storage: | 512GB | 
| OS: | Android 17 | 
| Primary camera: | 50MP (f/1.6) Sony Lytia 910 1/1.28-inch sensor w/ OIS | 
| Ultra-wide camera: | 50MP (f/2.0) 1/2.76-inch sensor | 
| Telephoto camera: | 200MP (f/2.6) 1/1.56-inch sensor | 
| Front Camera: | 16MP (f/1.9) 1/2.75-inch sensor | 
| Battery: | 7,000mAh | 
| Charging: | 90W wired, 50W wireless | 
| Colors: | Pantone Coal Smoke, Pantone Capulet Olive | 
Motorola Signature 27 review: Design
- Aluminum frame, material-effect back, glass-ceramic and brushed aluminum camera module
- Pantone Coal Smoke and Pantone Capulet Olive options
- IP69/IP68 dust- and water-resistant and MIL-STD-810H rated
The Motorola Signature 27's design will divide opinion. This in itself is a sign that a manufacturer is trying something different in a painfully samey industry, and is thus to be applauded.
I don’t think we need to stop at polite applause for effort, though. The Motorola Signature 27 looks stunning and feels even better, building upon the brand's distinctive previous work with ample curves and invitingly tactile materials.
While you get an ostensibly flat aluminum rim here, it’s not that of your average iPhone wannabe. There’s a tightly grooved finish that adds a note of premium gadgety class, not to mention added grip, while the edges have a pleasing chamfer that thickens around the camera module.
Said camera module is, I think, the source of debate over the Signature 27’s look. It gently bulges out from the rear of the phone like previous Motorola phones, but now covers the width of the device. Motorola's choice of materials is split between a strip of shiny glass-ceramic and a strip of brushed aluminum.
The Signature 27 also wears three of its camera lenses side by side (by side), giving off slight insecty vibes. Those with acute trypophobia may disagree, but I think it’s a strong look that makes full use of the available surface area while minimizing flat-surface rocking.
The rest of the rear surface pays tribute to Motorola’s work with material finishes. My stealthy Coal Smoke model adopts a tightly woven finish redolent of Kevlar or carbon fiber. It feels relatively resistant to fingerprints and nicks, at least compared to phones using more traditional glass materials.
I also spent a very small amount of time with the Pantone Capulet Olive model, which would be my preference thanks to its rich green color and warm fabric-like feel.
Whichever finish you opt for, this is a substantial phone. It doesn’t have an especially large footprint — at 162.01 x 77.04 x 7.99mm, it’s smaller than the iPhone 18 Pro Max — but a weight of 227g places it just a few grams south of the Oppo Find X10 Pro Max.
This is where Motorola’s design approach really comes good, because the Signature 27 wears that weight relatively lightly. The mix of materials and the use of assorted curves and angles means that it sits easily in the hand.
It feels dense and expensive — which, of course, it is — so it’s reassuring to note that the Signature 27 boasts both IP69 dust and water resistance and military-grade MIL-STD-810H certification. I’m still wary about how those exposed glass edges (front and back) would fare in a drop, but I’m not worried about how it’ll stand up to the day-to-day grind.
Motorola’s choice of a 2.5D Corning Gorilla Glass Ceramic 3 screen continues to run counter to the dead-flat majority, and it furthers the uniquely soft look and feel of the phone. It doesn’t hamper the viewing experience too much, though there are minor edge reflections to contend with if you’re of the ‘fill screen’ persuasion. I didn't detect any false palm inputs.
My main problem with Motorola’s display, from a design viewpoint, is a corner curve gradient that doesn’t match that of the frame. This leads to an uneven bezel thickness, which is a rare, less-than-premium touch — albeit a minor one.
- Design score: 5 / 5
Motorola Signature 27 review: Display
- 6.78-inch 120Hz LTPO OLED
- 1.5K Super HD (2772 x 1272)
- 12,000 nits peak, 3,000 nits HBM
- 2,160Hz PWM
The first thing you’ll notice about the Motorola Signature 27 is its bold new design, but the most consequential addition is its new display.
The phone uses a 6.78-inch OLED panel with a 2772 x 1272 (1.5K) resolution. LTPO technology allows for a variable refresh rate from 1 to 120Hz, while there’s also a 360Hz touch sampling rate and 2160Hz PWM Dimming. So far, this is a pretty ordinary flagship spec, and not what you’d necessarily think of as a best-in-class contender.
Where things get interesting is that this is the first phone ever to deploy Tandem OLED technology. We’ve seen this technique deployed before in Apple's latest MacBook Pro and iPad Pro devices, and it fulfils a similar function here. With two layers of OLED material, the Signature 27's display can get considerably brighter without demanding too much more from the battery.
In general terms, it produces an impressive top-level brightness of 3,000 nits in high brightness mode (HBM), making it eminently usable outdoors. That’s not even the headline spec, though.
Where the Signature 27 display really shines is in HDR content (Dolby Vision and HDR10+), where highlights can hit a staggering 12,000 nits. This extra level of peak brightness doesn’t exactly hit you around the head in day-to-day use, but the level of pop and contrast in high-quality visual content is truly impressive.
This is one of the cleanest, most vivid displays I’ve ever used, without straying into garish or unnatural territory — especially after switching to the Natural color mode.
- Display score: 5 / 5
Motorola Signature 27 review: cameras
- 50MP f/1.6 main (1/1.28-inch)
- 50MP f/2.0 ultra-wide (1/2.76-inch)
- 200MP f/2.6 3x telephoto (1/1.56-inch)
- 50MP f/1.9 selfie camera (1/2.75-inch)
Motorola didn’t used to be very good at cameras, but in the past couple of years it appears to have doubled down in this department. It’s paying dividends.
Following the Motorola Signature and Motorola Razr Fold, which deployed the same credible triple 50MP system, the Motorola Signature 27 takes things even further.
Joining the newly LOFIC-boosted 50MP 1/1.28-inch main sensor this time around is a new and much-improved 200MP 1/1.56-inch 3x telephoto camera. This joins a fairly bog-standard 50MP 1/2.76-inch ultra-wide and a 50MP selfie cam.
There’s a fourth sensor this time around, and it’s quite novel. The Signature 27 is the first phone to feature a dedicated EVS action sensor. This apparently helps the main image processor by detecting pixel-level changes in light, helping to capture movement better, even in lower-light conditions (further aided by 3.5-degree OIS).
A new Action Shot mode claims to utilize this sensor to capture fast-moving subjects. It successfully picked out several harborside shots that I took where seagulls were swooping across the shot at pace, freezing them mid-flight with minimal blur. Still, I can't say the Signature 27 performed noticeably better than its flagship rivals at capturing motion.
In general shooting, that LOFIC-enhanced main sensor captures seriously contrasty shots with deep shadows and vibrant highlights. They’re not always what you’d call 'natural' — I noticed a certain amount of extra color-pop when shooting on an unseasonably sunny day — but I generally found that this was more a case of a strong look than one of heavy-handed image processing.
Contemporaries might strike a more accurate tone in such amped-up scenarios, but I can’t deny that I really enjoyed the distinctively rich shots that the Signature 27 delivered. Night shots, too, produced plenty of detail, preserving that inky blackness.
Motorola includes a pair of preset styles and an AI-driven custom style that feeds off your photo edits. That’s a nice idea, but I’d like a few more properly calibrated options straight out of the box.
I did also note a couple of issues with autofocus when shooting close-up subjects. A couple of shots of beer glasses, for example, seemed to focus more on the bar, or otherwise failed to recognize the glass as the intended subject. Fingers crossed that this sort of thing can be ironed out in future updates.
The new telephoto is also capable of capturing excellent shots with admirable sharpness and contrast, especially at its native 3x and cropped 6x zoom levels. 10x shots are also solid, but I found the Signature 27 fell short of some of its premium rivals when it came to the more extreme AI-enhanced zoom lengths, right up to 100x blur-o-vision.

I wasn’t particularly enamored with the 50MP ultra-wide. It’s smaller and less pixel-packed than that of the Oppo Find 10 Pro Max — most ultra-wides are — but my main issue was that the tone occasionally wandered too far away from the main sensor, certainly in slightly murkier conditions.
The 50MP selfie camera produces solid results, though it isn’t in the same class as the Google Pixel 11 Pro's or iPhone 18 Pro's for detail and contrast. Video capture is nice and strong, extending to 8K at 30fps or 4K at 120fps.

All I can say is that I thoroughly enjoyed my time shooting with it, and that it produced a handful of genuinely excellent shots that I’ve already favorited in my personal collection.

Motorola Signature 27 review: performance
- Qualcomm Snapdragon 8 Elite Extreme Gen 6 chipset
- 12GB LPDDR5X RAM
- 512GB storage
- B&O-tuned speakers
Motorola has been somewhat frugal with the choice of processor in its recent flagship phones, dropping them short of the very best. That’s no longer the case, with the Motorola Signature 27 packing the Snapdragon 8 Elite Extreme Gen 6.
This is Qualcomm’s fastest chip, and it’s backed by 12GB of fast LPDDR5X RAM and a new ArcticMesh cooling system, complete with “diamond-infused” gel and a meaty new 8384mm2 vapour chamber.
What this all means is that — somewhat spartan RAM allotment aside — the Motorola Signature 27 is almost as fast as they come. Benchmark tests show it to fall just a tad short of the RedMagic 12 Pro in Geekbench’s CPU and GPU scores, which isn’t bad given that this is a dedicated gaming phone. It’s significantly faster than the Oppo Find X10 Pro Max, which is a more direct rival.
3DMark’s Wild Life Extreme GPU test results also show the Motorola to be fairly close to the RedMagic, and it even gets within 10% on stability — meaning the Motorola can keep up the pace reasonably well under a sustained load. The famously resource-hungry Wuthering Waves game defaulted to Quality graphical settings here with a smooth and consistent 30fps, and I was able to crank that frame rate up to a 60fps target with barely a stutter.
I didn’t notice the phone getting excessively hot, even across two lengthy camera workouts in which I shot hundreds of photos and a number of 4K videos. It'll warm up when fast-charging or playing games for a while, but nothing too extreme.
If you’ve been gawping at those close-ups of the Signature 27’s camera module, you’ll no doubt have noticed the B&O logo. Danish deluxe audio specialist Bang & Olufsen is lending its tuning expertise here, producing a clear, spacious sound output from a pair of coaxial stereo speakers.
It also supplies a range of mode presets, which meaningfully alter the sound profile to suit certain media types (music, films, games, etc.). You can also use B&O’s tool to tweak the sound profile yourself, adding bass or treble according to taste, and all of these EQ tweaks can be applied to your Bluetooth headset of choice.
I would have liked readier access to the different B&O modes, and maybe the ability to assign different presets to individual apps or media types. But overall, the Signature 27’s audio game is strong.
- Performance score: 4.5 / 5
Motorola Signature 27 review: software
- Android 17
- 7 years of software support
- New Qira AI assistant
- GrapheneOS support promised
Motorola has shown signs of diverging somewhat from its path of offering a clean take on Android, offering increased bloatware and taking a maddeningly lax approach to AI. The Signature 27 goes some way toward restoring its reputation.
This phone runs a fairly crisp take on Android 17, albeit one that now looks quite different from the one you’ll find running on, say, the Google Pixel 11 Pro XL. The icons are squarer, the font is Motorola’s own, and the notification bar has separated from the quick settings panel by default.
As with many other manufacturers, Motorola has implemented its own little take on Apple’s Dynamic Island system, providing heads-up widgets around the front camera for things like media players and timers. It’s handled with tasteful minimalism, though it's not as polished as Apple's original implementation.
The company has also implemented a new Daily Drops summary system, which works a lot like Samsung’s Now Brief to pull together personalized weather, schedule, and news information each morning. It’s not immediately apparent, nor can it be found with a system search, but you can customize this system in the Notifications section of the Settings menu.
All this is tweakable, of course, but even if you leave it all alone, Motorola’s work is pretty easy on the eye. Bloatware is now at a minimum, though FIFA Heroes, Amazon Music, Facebook, Instagram, and TikTok apps come pre-installed. Motorola still insists on loading up the Opera web browser alongside Chrome, too, which is never not going to rankle. But these are all easily ignored, and indeed deleted.
Mercifully, Motorola has stopped its short-lived practice of throwing multiple AI assistant apps at us to see what sticks (answer: none of them except good old Gemini). In their place comes a new home-brewed AI assistant called Qira, accessible (by default) with a long press of the action button on the left edge.
In practice, it’s mainly useful for things like meeting transcriptions and speedy contextual screen summaries. I found that most other tasks — from general AI queries to image generation — were generally better served by Gemini, which is of course also installed. Still, it represents welcome progress.
Elsewhere, Motorola is promising up to seven years of software updates, which is in the same vicinity as Google, Samsung and Honor. Rare support for the super-secure GrapheneOS is also promised, though there's nothing to test on that front just yet.
- Software score: 4 / 5
Motorola Signature 27 review: Battery life
- 7,000mAh battery
- 90W wired charging
- 50W wireless charging
Motorola has kept things blissfully simple with the Signature 27’s battery provision. You get a nice large 7,000mAh cell wherever you are in the world.
While not the biggest battery on the market, this remains a sizeable component, and it results in admirable stamina. I was never remotely concerned about the phone lasting until bedtime, even on extremely intensive days.
Indeed, on several occasions, I simply didn’t charge the Signature 27 up at the end of the day, and was able to coast through to the next evening. After a day chalking up just short of five hours of screen-on time — a pretty heavy day in my book, albeit with a fairly stable network environment — I still found myself with more than 60% in the tank.
This strong stamina is backed by speedy charging. There’s support for 90W wired charging, which will get you a full charge from empty in just under an hour — though you’ll need to supply your own brick.
There’s also rapid 50W wireless charging, if you have the necessary peripheral for the task. It’s a shame there’s no Qi2 support, though, considering Motorola dipped its toe into the magnetic attachment system with the Motorola Edge 70 Max.
You can use that extra battery capacity to help those with lesser phones, too, courtesy of 5W wireless reverse and 4.5W wired reverse charging.
- Battery score: 4.5 / 5
Should you buy the Motorola Signature 27?
| Motorola Signature 27 scorecard |  |  | 
|---|---|---|
| Attributes | Notes | Rating | 
|---|---|---|
| Design | The Signature 27 looks like no other phone on the market. It also feels as good as it looks, and features top-tier robustness certification. | 5 / 5 | 
| Display | As the first phone to employ Tandem OLED technology, the Motorola Signature 27’s screen is as vibrant as they come, outputting a stunningly vivid picture. | 5 / 5 | 
| Performance | There won’t be many faster phones launched over the coming 12 months, with Qualcomm’s latest flagship processor driving the Signature 27 on to great things. | 4.5 / 5 | 
| Camera | It isn’t the most balanced or consistent camera out there, but the Signature 27 is capable of taking sharp, contrasty shots with plenty of pop and personality. | 4 / 5 | 
| Battery | A large 7,000mAh battery produces genuine two-day stamina, while 90W wired and 50W wireless charging gets you back up to speed quickly. | 4.5 / 5 | 
| Software | Motorola has cut some of the flab, honed its UI, and focused on a single AI assistant — albeit one that most people will probably ignore. Seven years of support is up there with the best. | 4 / 5 | 
| Value | It costs significantly more money than its predecessor, but the Motorola Signature 27 is about the same price as the iPhone 18 Pro Max and quite a bit cheaper than the Oppo Find 10 Pro Max. | 3.5 / 5 | 
Buy it if...
You’re bored of modern smartphone design
The Motorola Signature 27 is the most interesting-looking (and -feeling) phone on the market, with a fresh look and warm textures. You’ll want to handle it even when you’re not using it.
You want the most vibrant picture possible
Tandem OLED technology makes this the best smartphone display for showing off HDR content — and just content in general. It’s a scorching display in more ways than one.
You want to follow the action closely
Motorola’s pioneering use of EVS action sensor technology enables the Signature 27 to capture moving subjects with precision.
Don't buy it if...
You’re strapped for cash
The Signature 27 isn’t the most expensive phone on the market, but it’s a lot more expensive than any non-foldable Motorola handset before it.
You like to travel light
It might be a looker, but the Signature 27 is also an undeniably heavy phone.
Motorola Signature 27 review: also consider
The Motorola Signature 27 is a distinctively luxurious phone, but there are alternatives out there for those after something a little extra.
iPhone 18 Pro Max
Apple wrote the book on phones with a sharp design and clean software, and the iPhone 18 Pro Max once again delivers on both fronts. It costs about the same, features even faster performance, and has a camera gimmick of its own in the form of a variable aperture.
Read our full iPhone 18 Pro Max review
Samsung Galaxy S26 Ultra
Samsung knows how to make a high-end ‘Ultra’ phone by now, and this one’s a doozy. It too has a unique screen feature in its anti-snoop Privacy Display, while it continues to be the only high-end phone with an integrated stylus. 
Read our full Samsung Galaxy S26 Ultra review
Oppo Find X10 Pro Max
What’s that? You want a big, compromise-free phone with epic battery life, but you want it to trade those showy looks for a better-rounded camera system? Meet the Oppo Find X10 Pro Max. You’ll have to pay out even more money, mind. 
Read our full Oppo Find X10 Pro Max review
How I tested the Motorola Signature 27
- Review test period = 1 week
- Testing included = Everyday use, including web browsing, social media, photography, video calling, gaming, streaming video, music playback
- Tools used = Geekbench 7, 3DMark, native Android stats
☑️ 100s of smartphones reviewed
☑️ 15 years of product testing
☑️ Over 16,000 products reviewed in total
☑️ Nearly 200,000 hours testing tech
I tested the Motorola Signature 27 as my own phone for a week. I played demanding titles like Wuthering Waves for extended periods, watched movies and TV shows on apps like Apple TV, and browsed the internet and social media during casual-use days.
I tested the phone's power credentials using benchmark apps including Geekbench 7 and 3DMark, and used a compatible Anker 150W power adapter to measure its charging speed.
First reviewed: November 2026
Jon is a freelance journalist who has been covering tech since the dawn of the smartphone era. Besides TechRadar, his words and pictures have appeared in The Telegraph, ShortList, Tech Advisor, Trusted Reviews, Expert Reviews, and more. He largely covers consumer technology, with a particular focus on smartphones and tablets. However, he's also been known to dabble in the worlds of entertainment and video games.
